findings.evidenceJa: 森の主であるイリヤの案内
findings.governingReading: They reach the exit early through the guidance of Illya, the forest’s mistress or master.
findings.explanation: The English omits her established relation to and authority over the forest.

findings.evidenceJa: 行きに使った車
findings.governingReading: The car used for the outbound journey to the forest has disappeared.
findings.explanation: “Arrived in” leaves the trip’s direction and destination ambiguous.

findings.evidenceJa: 泥だらけ傷だらけ
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Illya are covered in mud and wounds.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes both concrete conditions as filth and deletes their injuries.

findings.evidenceJa: 強盗みたいなヒッチハイク
findings.governingReading: Shirou marvels that he has resorted to hitchhiking like a robber while still alive.
findings.explanation: The English omits the comic criminal comparison.

findings.highlight: It was afternoon when I stepped into the house
findings.evidenceJa: 玄関に入るまでは夕方だった
findings.governingReading: It was evening until Shirou entered the foyer.
findings.explanation: The English moves the observed time earlier to afternoon.

findings.evidenceJa: 隣にいたイリヤ
findings.governingReading: Shirou addresses Illya who had been beside him, before discovering she is no longer there.
findings.explanation: The English makes her presently standing beside him, sharpening the spatial contradiction beyond his broken awareness.

findings.evidenceJa: まずは栄養をとる
findings.governingReading: Shirou said they should first take in nourishment.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes generic energy for nutrition.

findings.evidenceJa: おかげでいい思いしちゃった
findings.governingReading: Illya says she got a pleasant treat or benefited enjoyably from it.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the experiential reward to retrospective gladness.

findings.evidenceJa: 二人分の洗い物
findings.governingReading: The sink holds washing-up for two people.
findings.explanation: The English omits the count that evidences the meal Shirou cannot remember.

findings.evidenceJa: いっぱい買い物してきた
findings.governingReading: They got out in the shopping district and bought a large amount.
findings.explanation: The English weakens “a lot of shopping” into some groceries.

findings.evidenceJa: んそうだな
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s hesitation precedes “yeah.”
findings.explanation: The English fuses the interjection and response.

findings.highlight: I’m on the floor in my bedroom
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の部屋で倒れていた
findings.governingReading: Immediately after leaving the living room, Shirou finds himself collapsed in his own room.
findings.explanation: The English supplies the floor but omits the collapse.

findings.highlight: A sword’s pierced in my chest
findings.evidenceJa: 左の胸元に剣が刺さっている
findings.governingReading: The hallucinated sword is embedded in the left side of his chest.
findings.explanation: The English omits the side nearest the invading left arm.

findings.highlight: it feels like my life is draining out from it
findings.evidenceJa: ドクドクと血液のかわりに、生気が流出していっている
findings.governingReading: Life force seems to gush out in throbs in place of blood.
findings.explanation: The English omits the pulse and the explicit substitution of life force for blood.

findings.highlight: The left side of my chest is simply rebelling against my left arm
findings.evidenceJa: 左腕から伝わってくる違和感に、もっとも近い左胸が拒否反応を示している
findings.governingReading: The left chest, as the nearest area, is showing a rejection response to the abnormal sensation transmitted from the left arm.
findings.explanation: The English omits proximity and transmission and personifies the chest as rebelling against the arm.

findings.highlight: I can’t hold events in my mind unless I concentrate on them
findings.evidenceJa: 一部一部気を抜いて時間を過ごしていると、その間何が起きて何をしていたのかが、残らなくなっている
findings.governingReading: Whenever Shirou passes individual stretches of time with his guard down, no record remains of what happened or what he did.
findings.explanation: The English turns a newly observed episodic mechanism into a general inability to retain events without concentration.

findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮士郎
findings.governingReading: The written “self” carries a “memory” ruby: without conscious focus, the Emiya Shirou self/memory will disappear.
findings.explanation: The English supplies his name alone and loses the explicit overlap between selfhood and memory.

findings.highlight: Only pain or the utmost concentration
findings.evidenceJa: 胸を貫かれるほどの痛みか、それと同等の集中
findings.governingReading: Maintaining himself requires pain equivalent to having his chest pierced, or concentration equally intense.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the concrete pain threshold and relation between the two alternatives.

findings.evidenceJa: 気が緩んで映像が跳びそうになった時
findings.governingReading: He must wound his palm when relaxation threatens to make the experienced images skip.
findings.explanation: The English omits the perceptual warning sign and reduces the trigger to any relaxation.

findings.evidenceJa: いつかの水晶
findings.governingReading: He finds the crystal from some earlier occasion.
findings.explanation: The English adds a definite shared “that day” relation.

findings.highlight: not even enough for one strengthening magic
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の魔術一回分にも満たない
findings.governingReading: The remaining energy is insufficient for even one use of Shirou’s magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the comparison specifically to Strengthening.

findings.evidenceJa: あいつなら
findings.governingReading: Shirou still calls the school rescuer “that person,” leaving the recognition unstated.
findings.explanation: The English supplies female gender before he names or explicitly resolves the person.

findings.evidenceJa: 死にかけた人間を助ける
findings.governingReading: That person would save a human being on the verge of death even without a reason.
findings.explanation: The English abstracts the concrete dying person into “a life.”

findings.evidenceJa: 嬉しいコトとか楽しいコト
findings.governingReading: Thoughts that are happy or enjoyable make Shirou relax and nearly collapse.
findings.explanation: The English collapses the paired affective categories into one.

findings.evidenceJa: 最後の三回目は決定的になる
findings.governingReading: Shirou guesses the third Projection will be decisive, then separately fears his body will self-destruct.
findings.explanation: The English makes fatality certain before the following subjective qualification.

findings.highlight: an infinite number of blades will be created inside my body
findings.evidenceJa: 体内で無限の剣製が作られる
findings.governingReading: Unlimited Blade Works itself will be constructed inside Shirou’s body as Archer’s Reality Marble exceeds containment.
findings.explanation: The English turns the named internal world into merely an infinite quantity of blades.

findings.evidenceJa: 千の剣で串刺しにされて死ぬ
findings.governingReading: He will die impaled from within by a thousand swords.
findings.explanation: The English adds instant death.

findings.evidenceJa: それなりに受け入れてはいる
findings.governingReading: Shirou has accepted the hopeless facts only to some degree.
findings.explanation: The English changes qualified acceptance into acceptance of the whole situation.

findings.evidenceJa: 助かる
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists that he will survive or make it through.
findings.explanation: The English makes rescue or salvation passive.

findings.evidenceJa: 勝手にくたばっていい身分じゃない
findings.governingReading: After promising to protect Sakura, his body has no standing or permission to drop dead on its own.
findings.explanation: The English retains selfish death but loses the personified body and status/authorization logic.

findings.highlight: If she’s not doing well, I’ll need to look after her
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂がまいってたら手当てをしてやらないと
findings.governingReading: If Rin is physically overcome or debilitated, Shirou must give her treatment.
findings.explanation: The English weakens both her condition and concrete medical care.

findings.evidenceJa: ちょいちょい、と壁ぎわを指差す
findings.governingReading: Illya repeatedly flicks or beckons her pointing gesture toward the wall area.
findings.explanation: The English removes the small repeated motion.

findings.evidenceJa: ほんの一時間前
findings.governingReading: Rin arrived only one hour earlier.
findings.explanation: The English adds approximation and omits the “only” emphasis.

findings.highlight: I could’ve been taken to the Great Holy Grail and had my heart taken out at any time
findings.evidenceJa: 数分後には大聖杯に連れて行かれて心臓を抜き取られていてもおかしくなかった
findings.governingReading: Within minutes, Illya could plausibly have been taken to the Greater Grail and had her heart extracted.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the specific imminent interval with the unbounded “at any time.”

findings.highlight: A little strictness is just right for him
findings.evidenceJa: 人一倍厳しいぐらいが丁度いい
findings.governingReading: Shirou needs treatment stricter than what one gives other people.
findings.explanation: The English weakens exceptional strictness to a little strictness.

findings.highlight: I’ll be grateful if you see to that
findings.evidenceJa: わたしはもう安心かな
findings.governingReading: If Rin will be strict with Shirou, Illya says she can now rest easy.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her relief and implied transfer of responsibility with gratitude.

findings.highlight: I don’t think we would’ve made it
findings.evidenceJa: 間に合ったかどうか
findings.governingReading: Shirou leaves open whether departing for the forest now would have been in time.
findings.explanation: The English tilts the unresolved question into a negative judgment.

findings.evidenceJa: 重い選択
findings.governingReading: The forest forced Shirou into a grave, burdensome choice.
findings.explanation: The English weakens emotional and moral weight into importance.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂とイリヤの掛け合い
findings.governingReading: The back-and-forth interplay between Rin and Illya makes Shirou’s tension fade.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the relational exchange into any conversation.

findings.evidenceJa: アレが受胎してしまえば
findings.governingReading: Once Avenger is conceived or gestated within the Grail, Sakura will change completely.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the conception event and leaves “that” ambiguously pointing to birth or effort.

findings.evidenceJa: 聞きなれない言葉
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Rin frown at a term unfamiliar to them.
findings.explanation: The English makes the word intrinsically strange rather than new to the speakers.

findings.evidenceJa: それがアヴェンジャー
findings.governingReading: Illya identifies Avenger, then appositionally calls it the anti-hero summoned in the third ritual.
findings.explanation: The English fuses “Avenger” and “an.”

findings.highlight: an anti-hero that the Einzbern Master summoned
findings.evidenceJa: 喚んではいけなかった反英雄
findings.governingReading: It was an anti-hero that must never have been summoned.
findings.explanation: The English omits the explicit prohibition and resulting condemnation.

findings.highlight: I got the information out of Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: サクラから必要な情報を取り出して
findings.governingReading: Illya extracted the information necessary to understand the event from Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English omits that she took only necessary information, making the extraction sound unrestricted.

findings.evidenceJa: わたしがやるべき事
findings.governingReading: Illya has understood what she herself must do.
findings.explanation: The English redistributes her personal duty to the group.

findings.highlight: What, exactly, you’ve made into your enemy.
findings.evidenceJa: シロウたちが敵とみなしているモノ
findings.governingReading: Illya understands what the others regard as their enemy.
findings.explanation: The English suggests they actively made the entity into an enemy rather than classifying an existing threat.

findings.evidenceJa: 挑むように俺と遠坂を正視する
findings.governingReading: After a small breath, Illya looks Shirou and Rin squarely in the face as though issuing a challenge.
findings.explanation: The English omits the directness and challenging quality of her gaze.

findings.evidenceJa: 表向きの決まり事
findings.governingReading: Illya describes the ostensible rules of the Holy Grail War known to Shirou and Rin.
findings.explanation: The English changes the public rule structure into the war’s ostensible reason.

findings.evidenceJa: 七人の英霊を召喚して
findings.governingReading: The ritual summons seven Heroic Spirits, who become Servants through contracts.
findings.explanation: The English collapses the pre-contract Heroic Spirit category directly into Servants.

findings.highlight: become the hosts of the Servants
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊の依り代となり
findings.governingReading: Selected magi become yorishiro—vessels or anchors—for the Heroic Spirits.
findings.explanation: “Hosts” weakens the ritual receptacle function and again presupposes the Servant state.

findings.highlight: whether the summoner deserves the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を得る人間が相応しいかどうか
findings.governingReading: Heroic Spirits supposedly help determine whether the human who will obtain the Grail is worthy.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the candidate to the summoner, though the source states the eventual human recipient.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分たち以外の聖杯探求者
findings.governingReading: The contracted Heroic Spirits move to defeat every Grail seeker other than themselves.
findings.explanation: The English explicitly adds Servants as separate targets and recasts the broader seeker category.

findings.evidenceJa: 英霊
findings.governingReading: The written “Heroic Spirits” carries the Servant reading.
findings.explanation: The English fuses both layers without spacing into malformed “spiritsServants.”

findings.evidenceJa: なおこの世に干渉できる外界の力
findings.governingReading: Heroic Spirits embody power from outside that can nevertheless interfere with this world.
findings.explanation: The English preserves interference but omits the external power as their essence.

findings.evidenceJa: 現象を手に入れる為
findings.governingReading: The wars seek to obtain a miracle or phenomenon still beyond humanity.
findings.explanation: The English changes acquisition of a transcendent phenomenon into creating it.

findings.highlight: a soul of a mere human that’s fated to disappear from this world. Bringing it about is an act of God.
findings.evidenceJa: 肉体の死後に消え去り還り、この世から失われる“魂”を物質化する神の業
findings.governingReading: The divine craft materializes the soul of a mere human, which would otherwise disappear, return, and be lost from this world after bodily death.
findings.explanation: The English breaks the relation into fragments and never states that materializing the human soul is the divine act.

findings.evidenceJa: ま魔法って、あの魔法
findings.governingReading: Rin stammers over “Magic”—the marked category distinct from magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English fuses the stammer into “SSorceries” and pluralizes the category.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔法
findings.governingReading: The passage defines true Magic as mystery unreachable through magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English uses “sorcery,” destabilizing the fixed Magic/magecraft distinction.

findings.highlight: A divine mystery that cannot be reached with magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術では到達できない神秘
findings.governingReading: True Magic is mystery unattainable by magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English calls magecraft “magic,” reversing the modern fixed terminology at the very point the categories are contrasted.

findings.highlight: As I’m not even in the Association
findings.evidenceJa: 末端のそのまた末端、いや協会に属してもいない部外者
findings.governingReading: Shirou calls himself below even the lowest fringe member—indeed, an outsider who does not belong to the Association.
findings.explanation: The English preserves nonmembership but omits his emphatic double-low status.

findings.evidenceJa: 四人足らず
findings.governingReading: Fewer than four practitioners currently wield the five acknowledged Magics.
findings.explanation: The English changes a strict upper bound into approximation around four.

findings.evidenceJa: 英霊召喚の基盤
findings.governingReading: The foundation of Heroic Spirit summoning uses part of the Third Magic.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the named summoning foundation to an unspecified system.

findings.highlight: aren’t alive as part of this world or time
findings.evidenceJa: この地上に、この時代のモノとして生きている訳じゃない
findings.governingReading: Servants do not live on earth as beings belonging to this particular age.
findings.explanation: The English turns historical belonging into the abstract phrase “part of this world or time.”

findings.highlight: an existence of a higher dimension that can take a spirit form and still influence the physical world
findings.evidenceJa: 精神体でありながら単体で物質界に干渉できる、高次元の存在
findings.governingReading: The Third Magic creates a higher-dimensional being that, while remaining a spiritual body, can independently act upon the material world.
findings.explanation: The English changes persistent spiritual embodiment into an ability to take spirit form and omits independence.

findings.highlight: It takes a soul and elevates it to the next level of life.
findings.evidenceJa: 魂そのものを生き物にして
findings.governingReading: The art makes the soul itself into a living being, which then advances to the next stage.
findings.explanation: The English merges transformation and advancement, omitting the soul’s explicit conversion into life.

findings.evidenceJa: 次のステップって
findings.governingReading: Rin repeats “the next step” before reacting.
findings.explanation: The English fuses “step” and “that’s.”

findings.evidenceJa: 管理地
findings.governingReading: Illya refers to a managed magical territory capable of activating Magic.
findings.explanation: “Administrated land” is unnatural English.

findings.evidenceJa: 道が繋がっていないなら
findings.governingReading: If no path is connected, the founders must break through the wall themselves.
findings.explanation: The English changes absence of a connection into an existing path blocked by an obstruction.

findings.evidenceJa: 炉心
findings.governingReading: The Lesser Grail is the furnace core that powers the Greater Grail.
findings.explanation: The English modernizes the image into a nuclear-style reactor core.

findings.evidenceJa: “外部”からのマレビトである英霊
findings.governingReading: The ritual uses souls of Heroic Spirits specifically as visiting beings from outside.
findings.explanation: The English omits their marked marebito or outside-visitor status, which explains why their return opens the hole.

findings.evidenceJa: 望みのものは手に入らない
findings.governingReading: Opening the hole does not yet obtain the thing sought at the distant Root.
findings.explanation: The English reframes the founders’ desired object as an ordinary wish not being granted.

findings.evidenceJa: それでも聖杯を手にしたもの
findings.governingReading: Even so, whoever obtains the Grail gains inexhaustible magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English fuses “But” and “the.”

findings.highlight: The Holy Grail Wars must occur on a fifty-year cycle to accumulate enough mana
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯戦争が五十年周期なのは、英霊を召喚するだけの魔力を溜める為か
findings.governingReading: Rin infers or asks whether the fifty-year cycle exists to accumulate enough energy for Heroic Spirit summoning.
findings.explanation: The English turns her inference into a declarative fact before Illya confirms it.

findings.highlight: you need an incentive to summon the heroic spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊を召喚するには代償が必要
findings.governingReading: Summoning Heroic Spirits requires a price: their desires must be answered for them to respond.
findings.explanation: The English changes an exchange cost into motivational incentive.

findings.evidenceJa: 殺し合うって選定方法
findings.governingReading: The method of selection through mutual killing proved unexpectedly suitable.
findings.explanation: The English adds that the selected survivor is specifically the last magus, narrowing a method involving Masters and Servants.

findings.highlight: a power that governs dimensional theory
findings.evidenceJa: 次元論の頂点に在るという“力”
findings.governingReading: Mysticism posits a power situated at the apex of dimensional theory outside the world.
findings.explanation: The English makes the power govern a theory rather than occupy the cosmological apex the theory describes.

findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣だったら
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Kiritsugu would understand the Root’s importance.
findings.explanation: The English replaces his name with the familial role, changing the immediate callback and voice.

findings.evidenceJa: 協会
findings.governingReading: The Mage’s Association is a named institution.
findings.explanation: The English lowercases “association” in a setting-heavy exposition.

findings.highlight: Maybe I convinced her, because she shuts her mouth.
findings.evidenceJa: 痛いところをつかれたのか、遠坂はうっと黙り込む
findings.governingReading: Perhaps struck at a vulnerable point in her argument, Rin falls abruptly silent.
findings.explanation: The English turns discomfort at a pointed objection into possible persuasion and makes Shirou its direct cause.

findings.highlight: is this that Avenger thing? And he’s
findings.evidenceJa: その何かっていうのが復讐者ってヤツなのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether the unidentified something is Avenger and whether it resides in the Greater Grail.
findings.explanation: The English assigns male gender before this passage establishes the entity’s human origin.

findings.highlight: the souls of the heroic spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 無色の力である英霊たちの魔力
findings.governingReading: Avenger contaminates the Heroic Spirits’ magical energy, which is ordinarily uncolored power.
findings.explanation: The English changes magical energy into souls and omits its colorless baseline.

findings.highlight: a successful example of the Third Sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: 第三魔法の成功例になりつつある
findings.governingReading: Avenger is in the process of becoming a successful example of the Third Magic by taking form as life.
findings.explanation: The English declares it already successful and again substitutes Sorcery for Magic.

findings.highlight: The Holy Grail merely summoned an avenger
findings.evidenceJa: 大聖杯は第三魔法を成し得る復讐者を呼び出した
findings.governingReading: The Greater Grail merely summoned Avenger, whose nature can accomplish the Third Magic.
findings.explanation: The English names the Holy Grail rather than the Greater Grail, collapsing the two devices just distinguished.

findings.highlight: an avenger that can use the Third Sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: 第三魔法を成し得る復讐者
findings.governingReading: Avenger’s attribute allows it to accomplish or realize the Third Magic.
findings.explanation: The English makes Avenger a practitioner who can “use” Sorcery and changes the fixed term.

findings.evidenceJa: 英霊を召喚した
findings.governingReading: The desperate Einzberns summoned a Heroic Spirit specialized solely in killing.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the ritual category to a generic spirit.

findings.highlight: a foreign folklore they obtained, as catalyst
findings.evidenceJa: 異国の伝承を触媒にして
findings.governingReading: They use an old scripture and foreign legend as the summoning catalyst.
findings.explanation: The English uses uncountable “folklore” with an article and omits the article before “catalyst.”

findings.evidenceJa: 手の内にある中で最悪の魔
findings.governingReading: They summon the worst demon or magical evil available within their own holdings.
findings.explanation: The English removes the constraint of what the Einzberns possessed and broadens it to the worst evil possible.

findings.evidenceJa: 悪性の容認者
findings.governingReading: The character’s account calls Angra Mainyu the acceptor, acknowledger, or guarantor of evil.
findings.explanation: The English changes a relational role into literal embodiment of evil.

findings.highlight: Ahura Mazda, protector of human goodness
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の善性を守護する光明神
findings.governingReading: The Japanese calls the opponent a god of light who protects human goodness without naming it here.
findings.explanation: The English inserts “Ahura Mazda,” adding external identification to the character’s wording.

findings.highlight: its soul wouldn’t be compatible with the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯に相応しい魂
findings.governingReading: Rin argues such an unknown evil spirit could not possess a soul worthy of the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English changes worthiness into technical compatibility.

findings.evidenceJa: 絶対悪よ、リン
findings.governingReading: Illya answers Rin with the classification “absolute evil,” then explains the human bearer of the name.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the categorical answer with a repetition of the name and removes the concept that frames the explanation.

findings.highlight: a hero that lived in a small, nameless village
findings.evidenceJa: 村落に現れた英雄だった
findings.governingReading: Illya says the hero appeared in the nameless village.
findings.explanation: The English changes an appearance relation into residence.

findings.highlight: these people, segregated from the rest of the world
findings.evidenceJa: 貧しく、外界から隔離された彼ら
findings.governingReading: The villagers are poor as well as cut off from the outside world.
findings.explanation: The English removes the poverty that defines their narrow material world.

findings.highlight: the only source of human pride that they knew
findings.evidenceJa: 人間以下である彼らを人間たらしめる唯一の誇り
findings.governingReading: Their absolute prayer is the sole pride by which people described as less than human can make themselves human.
findings.explanation: The English reduces a harsh self-humanizing logic to the only kind of pride they happen to know.

findings.evidenceJa: 殺戮
findings.governingReading: Illya names slaughter among the human functions the villagers reject.
findings.explanation: The English euphemizes killing into general conflict.

findings.evidenceJa: 予め人に付属された機能すべてを否定して
findings.governingReading: The villagers reject all functions attached to human beings from the outset, including hunger, slaughter, love, and hate.
findings.explanation: The English calls the examples concerns and drops both their innate status and the totalizing rejection.

findings.highlight: From the moment we are born, there is evil in us
findings.evidenceJa: 悪とは元からあるもの
findings.governingReading: Illya says evil is something already there; the point is that righteous conduct alone cannot detach it.
findings.explanation: The English turns the proposition into an explicit claim that evil exists inside each person from birth.

findings.evidenceJa: 悪い事ができない
findings.governingReading: The villagers believe everyone remaining would be unable to do evil deeds.
findings.explanation: The English changes inability to commit evil into inability to be evil.

findings.evidenceJa: 人を呪うあらゆる言葉
findings.governingReading: They carve onto him every formula or word used to curse people.
findings.explanation: The English makes the words themselves cursed and obscures their directed function.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼らが知り得る全ての罪業
findings.governingReading: They impose every sin available to the villagers’ knowledge.
findings.explanation: The English expands a community-bounded inventory into every imaginable sin.

findings.highlight: held him responsible for all evils in the world
findings.evidenceJa: 全ての悪事を彼の責任とした
findings.governingReading: They make him responsible for every evil deed in their constructed world.
findings.explanation: The English explicitly expands the sentence to all evil in the world before the narration defines the village as a small complete world.

findings.highlight: They believed they were pure and righteous
findings.evidenceJa: 我々は何をしても善なる者だ
findings.governingReading: The villagers reason that whatever they themselves do, they remain good because all sin is located in him.
findings.explanation: The English states their claimed goodness but omits the license to commit any act without losing it.

findings.highlight: they continuously tortured one man until he went insane
findings.evidenceJa: 一人の青年を崩壊するまで殺し続けた
findings.governingReading: They keep killing the young man without granting death until his person is destroyed or collapses.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes torture ending in insanity, narrowing bodily and personal destruction to a mental outcome.

findings.highlight: until he succumbed to old age
findings.evidenceJa: その寿命がつきるまで
findings.governingReading: They refuse him death until his allotted life runs out.
findings.explanation: The English makes him die of old age, an unsupported naturalistic cause after prolonged ritual destruction.

findings.highlight: was irrationally hated by everyone in the world
findings.evidenceJa: 世界中の人間の敵として、ただ理不尽に殺され憎まれ続けた
findings.governingReading: He is constituted as all humanity’s enemy and continues to be killed and hated without reason.
findings.explanation: The English preserves hatred but removes both his imposed enemy status and the continuing killing.

findings.evidenceJa: 世界中の人間の善性を証明してくれる
findings.governingReading: The victim is revered as proof of the goodness of people throughout the world.
findings.explanation: The English restricts the proof to the villagers’ own goodness.

findings.highlight: His existence pardoned everyone of their evil deeds
findings.evidenceJa: どんなに人々が悪事を重ねようとも『清く正しい』と赦される免罪符
findings.governingReading: His existence acts as an indulgence by which people are declared “pure and righteous” however many evil deeds they accumulate.
findings.explanation: The English retains pardon but removes the continuing accumulation and the villagers’ false positive judgment of purity.

findings.highlight: a curse made by a concept of ancient people
findings.evidenceJa: 原初の人の想念が作り上げた、“願い”という名の呪いのカタチ
findings.governingReading: Angra Mainyu is the form of a curse called a “wish,” produced by primordial human thought.
findings.explanation: The English loses the crucial identity of wish and curse and reduces active collective thought to a vague ancient concept.

findings.highlight: A human who everyone wanted to represent their evil
findings.evidenceJa: この世の悪であれと望まれた人間
findings.governingReading: He is a human whom others wished to be the evil of this world.
findings.explanation: The English makes him represent people’s own evil, weakening the imposed universal role that the Grail later accepts.

findings.highlight: He was merely constructed by the people around him
findings.evidenceJa: 周りの人間の想いだけで構成された、有り得ない筈のモノ
findings.governingReading: He is an entity that should not exist, constituted solely by the thoughts of those around him.
findings.explanation: The English preserves construction by others but removes both its sole material and its impossibility.

findings.evidenceJa: 方向性のない魔力
findings.governingReading: Defeated Servants return as magical energy without direction or purpose.
findings.explanation: The English calls the energy raw but removes the lack of direction that distinguishes normal stored power from Angra Mainyu’s imposed wish.

findings.highlight: a heroic spirit that others wished for
findings.evidenceJa: 周りが願って創り上げた英雄
findings.governingReading: Angra Mainyu is a hero created by the wishes of people around him.
findings.explanation: The English says only that others wished for a heroic spirit, obscuring that their wish constructed him and survives the loss of personality.

findings.highlight: He was a mere human, but wasn’t treated as one
findings.evidenceJa: 性別も人格も、人でさえないソレ
findings.governingReading: After reduction in the Grail, the entity has neither sex nor personality and is no longer even human.
findings.explanation: The English instead repeats his former humanity and social mistreatment, deleting his present ontological state.

findings.evidenceJa: 人々が望んだ姿で生まれる事になった
findings.governingReading: Inside the Grail, the fabricated heroic spirit is set to be born in the form people desired.
findings.explanation: The English reports embodiment as already granted and omits the determining form of the surrounding wish.

findings.highlight: an ideal human that has been wished for since the age of gods
findings.evidenceJa: 神代から願われてきた“人間の理想”
findings.governingReading: The wish is “humanity’s ideal,” desired since the Age of Gods: the removal or externalization of evil.
findings.explanation: The English turns an ideal held by humanity into an ideal specimen of a human being.

findings.evidenceJa: あの影の本体
findings.governingReading: Illya identifies the true body or underlying entity of the shadow.
findings.explanation: The English equates the explanation directly with the shadow and loses the body/manifestation distinction.

findings.highlight: It finally obtained form as a heroic spirit
findings.evidenceJa: ようやくカタチを得ようとするモノ
findings.governingReading: The entity is only now trying or about to attain form as a heroic spirit.
findings.explanation: The English makes the formation complete, contradicting the later insistence that birth can still be prevented.

findings.evidenceJa: ただ悪であれ、と
findings.governingReading: The phrase restates the bare injunction or wish imposed on Angra Mainyu: be evil.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the desire to Angra Mainyu himself, reversing the agency central to Illya’s account.

findings.evidenceJa: 宝具を備えたサーヴァント
findings.governingReading: The incarnating Servant is equipped with a Noble Phantasm capable of cursing all six billion people.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a defined Servant-system category with a generic ability.

findings.highlight: The contents of the Holy Grail have already been tainted by him
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯の中身はとっくにそいつに占拠されてて
findings.governingReading: Rin first asks whether the Grail’s contents have long since been occupied or taken over by him, then corrects herself to the wish being fixed.
findings.explanation: The English replaces occupation with contamination and blurs the self-correction’s precise distinction.

findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯の外に出ようとしていた“黒い影”
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu judged dangerous the black shadow that was trying to emerge from the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English makes the shadow passive leakage and removes its directed approach toward birth.

findings.highlight: the Angra Mainyu that formed inside the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯によって受肉するアンリマユ
findings.governingReading: Illya distinguishes the former human from the Angra Mainyu that will be incarnated by the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English changes future incarnation through the Grail into formation already completed inside it.

findings.highlight: use Sakura to obtain Angra Mainyu
findings.evidenceJa: サクラを餌にして、“この世全ての悪”を釣り上げたい
findings.governingReading: Zouken means to use Sakura as bait to fish “all the world’s evil” out of the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English retains instrumental use but removes the bait-and-extraction mechanism and Illya’s contemptuous image.

findings.highlight: the taint of the magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: アンリマユからの魔力汚染
findings.governingReading: Sakura cannot withstand magical-energy contamination coming specifically from Angra Mainyu.
findings.explanation: The English makes the contamination generic and drops its source.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分の魂の容れ物である本体
findings.governingReading: Illya says Zouken can possess any human body so long as his true body, the vessel of his soul, exists.
findings.explanation: The English supplies a worm as the referent and removes the explicit distinction between his true body and borrowed bodies.

findings.evidenceJa: 魂が物質化した架空の魔物
findings.governingReading: Zouken ultimately plans to transfer into an imaginary monster whose soul has materialized.
findings.explanation: The English names Angra Mainyu directly and removes the description of the prospective body’s ontological state.

findings.highlight: a soul given flesh is a living example of the Third Sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: 第三魔法の成功例、魂が物質化した
findings.governingReading: Materialization of the soul makes the target a successful instance of the Third Magic.
findings.explanation: The English changes successful instance into “living example” and uses unstable Magic terminology.

findings.highlight: tainting a perfect god with one’s own human desires
findings.evidenceJa: 完全な神を、人間が自らの欲望で不完全な神に貶める
findings.governingReading: Illya compares Zouken’s plan to humans degrading a perfect god into an imperfect god through their desire.
findings.explanation: The English says only that the god is tainted, losing the resulting imperfect divinity and the downward transformation.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s creation will take many lives
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の代行者として、多くの命を奪う
findings.governingReading: What Sakura produces will take lives as her proxy or agent.
findings.explanation: The English preserves causal creation but removes the proxy relation that makes Shirou frame the deaths as Sakura’s burden.

findings.evidenceJa: 寄り代である桜
findings.governingReading: Rin’s first option is to kill Sakura in her role as the vessel or anchor before “all the world’s evil” emerges.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes her Master status, obscuring why killing her body can prevent emergence.

findings.highlight: We won’t be able to do it without defeating them
findings.evidenceJa: 二人を避けて大聖杯は破壊できない
findings.governingReading: Rin says the Greater Grail cannot be destroyed while avoiding Sakura and Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English promotes unavoidable confrontation into a requirement to defeat both of them.

findings.evidenceJa: それが桜のいる世界
findings.governingReading: Shirou calls the underground cavern “the world Sakura inhabits,” a loaded formulation after her isolation and transformation.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the line to her physical location and removes Shirou’s characterization of her enclosed world.

findings.evidenceJa: わずかに息を吐いて
findings.governingReading: Shirou lets out a slight breath after sustained concentration.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the small release with a deep inhalation or full breathing action.

findings.evidenceJa: さっきの考えをより明確に纏めてくれる
findings.governingReading: The pendant’s cold touch lets Shirou assemble his preceding thought more clearly.
findings.explanation: The English renders emotional or mental settling and loses the clarification of a specific prior conclusion.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂に言った言葉に嘘はない
findings.governingReading: Shirou says the words he spoke to Tohsaka—agreeing to fight Sakura—were not a lie.
findings.explanation: The English assigns truthfulness to Tohsaka and breaks the bridge into Shirou’s private save-Sakura qualification.
